   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: G.W. North, BEXHILL ON SEA

I've two problems on which your
help would be much appreciated.
Problem 1: CATLOADER(+D Version)
in OUTLET Issue No. 44. Although
having much used this program, I
have never succeeded in the
option to load the "SYSTEM" file
but all other options work O.K.
Reading the instructions line
6350:2 which reads...
"SYSTEM" CODE NOT PI, VAL "6656"
is made to VAL "8912,6656" and
re-saved as "AUTOLOAD".

However, using the program to
format, load CATLOADER and
system file results in the error
report"nonsense in BASIC 6350:2"
on a fresh disc.

The formatting is O.K. as well
as loading of CATLOADER but no
system file. Using "ORGANISER"
to load system file rectifies
matters. What is this old codger
doing wrong in his dotage?

Problem 2: is that recently my
SPECTRUM +2 (Grey case Amstrad
version) went on the blink and
as I am so dependant on it I
rashly bought a locally advert-
ised one with 60 terrible games
thrown in.

I should have been suspicious of
the black case but as it seemed
in good condition I bought it.
The truth dawned later and as
you may well guess was not a +2
but a +2A which as it stood
wouldn't work with the +D Drive.

A most helpful chat with DATEL
resulted in the return by next
post of their "Fixer" Board
which certainly allowed the +D
to work.

Believing that +3 BASIC was the
same as 128 BASIC on the +2
caused me try it out. With the
+2, if 128 BASIC is selected and
the disc is booted by typing
"run", the computer is then in
128 mode after pressing "space".
Whereas,with the Spectrum 2A and
+D, selecting +3 BASIC causes
the +2A to revert to 48 BASIC.
Again ?????. The happy end to
this saga is the trusty old +2
now seems O.K.

                  G.W. North

Brian Cavers to George North


What is confusing in CATLOADER
is that I have used "NOT PI" to
represent zero and VAL"" at the
save code line 6350 both to save
memory. To convert from saving
the Disciple DOS to saving the
+D DOS change...


"SYSTEM" CODE NOT PI, VAL "6656"

              to...

"+SYS 2a" CODE 8192, VAL "6656"

The filename should, of course,
be whatever filename you have
for your DOS version.

Regarding using the +D with +3
BASIC,read Susan Harvey's letter
in last month second batch of
OUTLETTERS, Page 4. Susan says
first load the system file then
enter...

 POKE @ 4426,16 : POKE @ 4427,92

       ...and reset the computer
to +3 BASIC. This should enable
you to use the +3 BASIC editor
as well as the +D.

                        - Brian

          Paul Preston,

In OUTLET Issue 054 - Outletters
page 3,Tony Catts wanted a prog-
ram to transfer files from Opus
disk to tape. Well, a program
has already appeared in OUTLET
to do this.It's called TRANSBACK
and was programmed by myself. It
is in OUTLET 27 and OUTLET Extra
No.01.

In OUTLET 53 you used my T3PRINT
program. What I do not think I
made clear was that it can be
used with any drive system by
altering the syntax to open a
file to your system and open a
printer stream.

The machine code only moves data
from one stream to another and
returns to BASIC if a graphic
character is encountered. Orig-
inally this was done in BASIC
using INKEY$ but the printer
ended up waiting for data to
print! Printing was actually
faster than moving data from one
stream to another in BASIC.

Just for interest here is the
source listing for the T3PRINT
code...

       ORG  23296
LCOUNT DEFB 0
PGLEN  EQU  78
START  DI
       LD   H,B
       LD   L,C

       DEC  BC
       LD   DE,1+NLINE-START
       ADD  HL,DE
       LD   (HL),C;
       INC  HL    ;code is
       LD   (HL),B;relocatable
       INC  HL    ;so alter
       INC  HL    ;lcount
       INC  HL    ;address see
       LD   (HL),C;label NLINE
       INC  HL    ;
       LD   (HL),B
LOOP   LD   A,4
       CALL 1601H;ROM  make
       stream 4  current channel
       CALL 15E6H;ROM wait key
       JR   C,ON ;valid char
       JR   NZ,EOF
ON     CP   13
       JR   Z,NLINE
       CP   127

       JR   NC,GRAPH
PRINT  EX   AF,AF'
       LD   A,3   ;make printer
       CALL 1601H ;current
       EX   AF,AF';channel
       RST  10H
       JR   LOOP
EOF    LD   BC,0
       RET
NLINE  LD   A,(LCOUNT)
       INC  A
       LD   (LCOUNT),A
       CP   PGLEN
       LD   A,13
       JR   NZ,PRINT
       LD   BC,12
       RET
GRAPH  LD   C,A
       LD   B,0
       RET

          R.O.M. Humour
Just to prove Dave Corney, the
Opus ROM author had a sense of
humour, read the error report
after running the following...

10 CLEAR #: OPEN #2;"#";2
20 PRINT

This program tries to enter an
infinite loop by redirecting
output to the screen again and
again. For those with the Opus
ROM disassembly refer to address
087Eh.
             CAT Bug
Like most large programs the
Opus ROM is not bug-free. When
performing a CAT that is longer
than the screen the 'scroll ?'
prompt appears.

Do not ever press a combined key
such as Cap shift 9 or graph key
etc., as the catalogue routine
gets confused and prints random
rubbish or worse still - it can
CORRUPT the catalogue! This is
due to Dave Corney not preserv-
ing the DE register pair when
calling the Spectrum PRINT-A-2
(15F2h). Those with an Opus ROM
disassembly refer to 0C3Bh.

    STOP PRESS    STOP PRESS
I've been after an Opus conver-
sion of Ocean IQ Laser Genius
machine code development system.
I couldn't get hold of one so I
sat down and converted it. I've
converted the assembler and
monitor/analyser completely in
machine code so the following
functions now work:-

            Assembler

 SAVE,LOAD,VERIFY,CODE,*INCLUDE,
*OPENOUT,CAT,ERA,EXPORT bug
cured and it prints via the Opus
printer port.

        Monitor/Analyser

SAVE,LOAD,FLIST,ERA,CAT,DEFSAVE,
DEFLOAD,ROM ON,ROM OFF,single
step Opus ROM and prints via
Opus printer port.

See my advert in OUTBOARD if you
want to order (you need the
original software).

        Yours sincerely,

          Paul Preston

Brian Cavers to Paul Preston

Thanks, Paul. I'd completely
forgotten about your TRANSBACK
program! Hopefully, readers can
still make good use of it and
haven't already laboured too
much to do the job manually!

In fact, I ought to use TRANS-
BACK myself for transferring
contrbutions from Opus disc.I do
have a routine but yours may be
better.
                       - Brian

From: M.D. Atkins, BURY

Dear Sirs,

Is it possible to obtain a tab-
loid printout on A4-sized paper?
I have tried this option and
keep getting 85 lines printed on
the one sheet and then only 6
lines on the next.

I can answer part of James
Castle's query regarding MASTER-
FILE +3 which is mentioned in
Les Tyler's letter. A file
created by MF+3 must fit in RAM,
therefore the capacity of any
one file is limited to the
Spectrum RAM disc space rather
than real disc capacity. So MF+3
can use up to 62K of the RAM
disc on the Spectrum +3.

Before I acquired MF+3 I had
been using version 04 on the 48K
Spectrum and had built up a few
files. These were saved as
character arrays and there was
no export option. However, MF+3
comes with a utility called CONV
which will process all files
produced by versions 01 to 09
and produce ASCII data files
which can then be imported into
MF+3. Incidentally MF+3 is now
marketed by Tasman Software.

        Yours faithfully,

           M.D. Atkins

Brian Cavers to M.D. Atkins

Most of us use A4 size paper but
I suspect your problem may be
that you are using CUT-SHEET
paper, that is,individual sheets
that you place in one at a time
or with a sheet-feed rather than
continuous perforated or roll
paper.

I looked into this and was very
surprised to find that, because
TABLOID crams in a lot of lines
on each page, single sheets of
paper run past the"end-of-paper"
detector which most printers use
to stop printing on the roller.
This means single-sheet paper
cannot easily print on the last
few lines.

I don't recall anyone else hav-
ing this problem which is rather
amazing really -unless they have
written and didn't mention they
used single sheets or unless I
misunderstood the problem!

In any event, I think I have now
cracked it and have added an
extra option in our print
routines from this issue onward.
The new option is on the printer
menu in text mode. Select CUT
SHEET for single sheets and the
option changes to CONTINUOUS to
switch back again. The routine
suppresses the end-of-paper
sensor but YOU MUST WIND DOWN
EACH SHEET TO BARELY JUST ABOVE
THE PRINT HEAD to get all the
text onto the sheet! Let me know
how you get on!          - Brian

From: G. Yeardley, CAMBRIDGE
        Tel:  0223-841946

Dear Ron and Brian,

I am trying to link up my Plus 3
with a JUKI 6100 parallel daisy-
wheel printer but without
success.

I have a parallel lead with a
centronics plug one end using
the printer port the Spectrum
end.Nothing happens on an LPRINT
or LLIST command.

I have seen this printer working
with a BBC B micro just using
the parallel printer command
*FX5,1. I have been told that
Spectrums don't work with daisy-
wheel printers. Is that correct?

Maybe one of your readers have
this set up and could help. I've
included my home 'phone number
just in case.

        Yours sincerely,

           G. Yeardley

Brian Cavers to Graham Yeardley

Yes, daisy-wheel printers most
definitely DO work on Spectrums!
They cannot, of course, print
high-res graphics but do accept
normal Epson commands the same
as any dot-matrix printer. You
may have one of the +3's with a
notorious printer bug. This is
cured in OUTLET so try printing
this page now to see if it is
O.K. If so, extract the routine
in the "DISK" program from line
1001 or 1002 (I forget which but
I'm sure it is marked) and use
it in your programs. If this
does not work you may have...
(1) a fault in the cable,
(2) a fault in the Spectrum or
(3) a fault in the printer.

You say you've seen the printer
working on a BBC. Do you mean
that individual printer or a
printer of the same model? Even
if it is the same printer it is
possible a fault crept in since
then.

However,this is less likely than
a cable fault or a Spectrum one.
You may need to check with a
repair shop.

Incidentally, you must be in 128
mode to print - not 48K.

You asked for our PD list. We
have no separate list but I have
now sent you our back issue list
but let me know if it's not yet
arrived!
                       - Brian

From: R. Barnes, WESTBURY

Hello chaps,

Thanks for the regular OUTLET,
keep up the good work.
1) I am looking for a more
readable character set for my
Tasword Plus 3. Currently, I
have to use both 'Wordmaster'and
'Tas+3' in the business for
different reasons. If you had
told me that I could handle two
different WP systems with ease I
wouldn't have believed it.

However, needs must as the devil
drives. I use your minichars W
in 'Wordmaster' and apart from
the missing 'dots' over the
'i's,which I find a problem when
proof-reading,it's pretty good.

The font which appears in a
photo to be the most readable is
the one used in the now defunct
'Spectral Writer' although I
have never seen it on the
screen.

Have you got a good font in
'Minichars' 2, 3 or 4 or what
have you that will load into
'Tasword +3'?

I enclose a cheque for `3.50
perhaps you will send the one
you consider the most readable.

 2) I've just come round to
thinking of computer advertising
again. So I bought 'Flexipage',
'PAWS', '3D Constructor Kit' and
have resurrected 'DLAN' from the
top of the cupboard.

My programming expertise is
virtually nil. I just don't get
enough opportunity to keep in
practice. So every time I sit
down to program I find I've
forgotten what I learnt last
time - three months ago!

When looking at a project like
this I decide what would be nice
and then scan through books,
discs and tapes to see what I
can cobble together. This time I
thought I'd like to horizontally
scroll a screen in sections at
various speeds. So I dug out
'Window Winder' by Paul Hiley
(Issue 11) and got stuck in. In
your blurb you said it's easy to
use.It might be to you,mate, but
I didn't even reach first base.

So, I dug out 'Banneroll' and
got to just about the same
place. I've already cobbled
together a good screen to scroll
from Flexipage and your Clipper.

 1) It was then that it dawned
on me that there was a yawning
gap in my knowledge which does
not seem to be covered anywhere.

Just how do you handle a screen
(one that you have prepared
earlier) in the context of a
larger program eg.'Window
Winder','Art program' etc? When
and where do you load it in the
program context? How do you stop
it being wiped off when the next
program line occurs? Do you
store it for recall, and if so,
where?

For instance when you use
'Window Winder' - do you load it
or merge it, before or after the
winding subroutine? When do you
activate all the Randomize
Usr's?

No matter where I do it I keep
losing the screen. How about a
short "teach-in" on screen
handling techniques in the
context of screen modifying
programs?

Am I being unduly thick or have
I missed some vital piece of
reading somewhere? Please can
you point me in the right
direction?

            R. Barnes

Brian Cavers to R. Barnes

Well, I drug out my old copy of
Tasword +3 and hacked through
the code but I could not find a
sign of the character set so I
can't advise how to load a new
character set or even if the
ones we have are suitable. I
can't remember if this problem
has come up in OUTLETTERS before
this. Has anyone else managed to
load a new character set into
Tasword +3?

Regarding including screens in
programs I assume you mean how
do you restore a picture to the
screen after something else has
replaced it, say, after printing
text or a CLS...

The easy way is to use HOLD IT
(OUTLET 24).After loading it you
press E to extract two lines
which you then save on disc or
tape. Whenever you want to store
a screen in a program you MERGE
in those two lines and then use:

10 LOAD "PICTURE" SCREEN$ : REM
   this is just after loading
   the program

20 GOSUB 9944 : REM this stores
   the screen in memory

30 rest of program which may
   clear the screen or PRINT on
   it or whatever.....

99 GO SUB 9946: REM this will
   restore the picture whenever
   you want it!

Regarding WINDOW WINDER (OUTLET
11), you extract the code lines
from the main demo program using
the Option in the main menu and
save that piece of BASIC. You
then MERGE it in your own prog-
rams as needed.


At the start of your program you
need a GO SUB 9930 to install
the code. I think there may be a
CLEAR command before that but it
will tell you in the instruct-
ions. To actually use it to
scroll part of a screen you need
to first tell the program WHICH
area or "window" of the screen
you want to scroll. You do this
using the POKEs listed in the
instructions: 65020 to 65023.

Having done that you now use one
of the RANDOMIZE USR calls as
described in the instructions
and the area you have POKEd will
scroll in one direction.You keep
repeating the RANDOMIZE USR to
scroll it more and more. Here's
an example...


10 CLEAR (whatever): GO SUB 9930

20 FOR N=1 TO 50: PRINT RND;
   :NEXT N: REM this just fills
   the top of the screen with
   numbers to test it, you could
   load a SCREEN$ instead

30 POKE 65020,0:POKE 65021,0:REM
   top left corner of screen at
   PRINT position 0,0.

40 POKE 65022,10:POKE 65023,10:
   REM make window area 10 by 10

50 FOR N=1 TO 100

60 RANDOMIZE USR 65000: REM
   scroll UP

70 PAUSE 0:REM wait for keypress

80 NEXT N



The above program should print
some random numbers then scroll
a few of them in the top left
corner of the screen UP. If you
then keep pressing a key they
will scroll up more and more up
to 100 times.

Now experiment with this simple
example until you master it. If
you have a particular program
problem then give me details and
I'll be happy to try to help
further.
                        - Brian.

From: Jon Westgate, GERMANY

Dear Ron and Brian,

Firstly my apologies that I have
used WordMaster to write this
text, but I have no other word
processor.

In the Feb. issue of OUTLET you
mentioned in an answer to Colin
Macdonald that many of the high-
res screens that are included in
OUTLET are ported across from
ST, Amiga or PC's.

Could you suggest what software
could be used to port eg. TIFF
or TGA files from PC's to SAM,
or must one write his own
conversion routine?

I am assuming I can actually get
the files from the PC to SAM
either by transferring via the
serial port, or by using a pack-
age such as the PC Suite from SD
Software. I see the main problem
in the conversion itself, with
the differing resolution and
number of colours. Any help or
suggestions would be greatly
appreciated.

In the same issue, in your reply
to Stuart Burton on the question
of transferring Spectrum micro-
drive programs to SAM, you
queried whether the Messenger
and Interface 1 clash. I have
done this many times with an
almost 100 percent success rate,
however it is IMPERATIVE to
observe the following:

Load the Spectrum program from
microdrive and then REMOVE the
microdrive cartridge before
going any further! Now load the
Messenger code into the SAM. At
this point you can press the
button on the Messenger. The
Spectrum screen will start to
flash and the MICRODRIVE WILL
START TO RUN! If a cartridge has
been left in the drive it will
be totally ERASED! Now you can
start the transfer by selecting
H from the SAM Messenger menu.

This method appears to work
successfully, however, I am not
sure what the long term effects
are on the Microdrive's whizzing
around with no cartridge loaded
while the transfer is taking
place.

To stop the Microdrive, reset
the Spectrum and type in CAT 1,
or switch off the power.

I hope this will be of some
help.

Keep up the excellent work and
my best wishes,

          Jon Westgate


Brian Gaff to John Westgate

Thank you for the Messenger
information, it should help a
lot of those who were dithering
about getting one. The spinning
drive should not damage itself.
I have had this situation many
times through faulty programm-
ing. Once back in Basic, typing
STOP usually stops it. I suspect
it occurs due to the Messenger
doing an OUT that happens to do
odd things to Interface one.

Getting onto your other point
about translating screens, this
is not that easy! I do not know
about TIFFs or TGAs, but I did
download a file describing GIF
format, and decided it was
beyond me!

It would no doubt be possible,
given enough detail on the
formats, but as these files tend
to be rather large, I fear the
manipulation would be best done
on the PC.

Transferring the code is fairly
easy. You could use the suite
you mention - this would be the
easier approach - or send it via
the RS232. Some comms I/Fs do
have quirks though.

I will have a hunt around the
text file areas on BBs for
screen file descriptions, and
let you know what I find.

                BG

From: Keith Pirie, ABERDEEN

Dear Cavers boys,

Thanks for Disk 54. Up to the
usual high standard but,Oh Dear!
One minor problem. I always look
forward to viewing the SCREEN$
files. Imagine my surprise when
I view "Fame" in that Issue and
I recognise it as one of the
files currently available on the
"People and Places 1" clip art
collection offered by my comp-
any: Teachers Pet.

Mr. Clayton ordered the collect-
ion in November 1990 and it was
supplied to him on microdrive at
a reduced cost, as I honoured
misprinted information in an
advert to which he responded.

I have no objections to the
SCREEN$ being used in purchasers
programs or newsletters etc.
(after all that is what they are
designed for) but I do object to
customer's presenting them as
their own work and (perhaps)
receiving payment for same.

I know you make payments for
contributions you use and I am
unsure what you may wish to do
about recovering any outlay you
may have made. It is impossible
for you to know which contrib-
utions are genuinely the work of
the submitters. The responsibil-
ity lies with them to be honest.
It is unfortunate that you are
occasionally let down by some.
All the best with future issues

Brian Cavers to Keith Pirie


Thanks, Keith.

This is an important point and I
thought it should be published.

I am certain that Chris Clayton
would have sent the screen to us
in all innocence believing it to
be public domain as there are so
many public domain clip art
screens around now. When I get
public domain programs or art
from third parties (i.e., not
orginal to the sender) I do not
usually make any payment and I
am sure, none was expected. This
was the case in the present
situation.

It is worth noting that the clip
art, instead of being marked:-
"by...", was marked, in the
Spectrum version:"SENT IN by..."
and in the SAM version as:-
"FROM..."(this slight change was
probably because I just grabbed
the BASIC from a previous SAM
clip art program instead of
converting the Spectrum BASIC
again). There was no intent to
claim that it was Chris's own
work nor did he represent it to
me as his own work at any time.

I am sorry this has happened and
the lesson is that readers must
be alert that they do not
contribute anything to OUTLET
unless it is their own work or
they know it to be in the public
domain (FREEWARE).      - Brian

From: D. Graham, BURNLEY

Dear Ron,

At present I have a +3 and a 48K
Spectrum+ with an Opus Discovery
1 single-sided disc drive.

Could you let me know if it is
possible to connect my Opus to
the +3? If so what connections
would I need?

Thank you once again.

        Yours sincerely,

            D. Graham

Brian Cavers to D. Graham

No, there is no practical way.In
theory,anything can be connected
to anything but just to give you
an idea... The +3 would need its
own power supply as the one in
the Opus is not sufficient so
you would need to cut the power
line on the edge connector. It
might then be possible to conn-
ect them using a FIXIT hardware
connector modified by someone
with a lot of electronic knowhow
and experience. Even then it
would only work in 48K mode and
there is no guarantee it would
work anyway. An electronics
enthusiast might tackle it out
of interest but otherwise I'd
leave it alone.
                     - Brian.

10 LOAD "PICTURE" SCREEN$ : REM this is just after loading the program

20 GOSUB 9944 : REM this stores the screen in memory

10 CLEAR (whatever): GO SUB 9930

40 POKE 65022,10:POKE 65023,10: REM make window area 10 by 10

50 FOR N=1 TO 100

60 RANDOMIZE USR 65000: REM scroll UP

70 PAUSE 0:REM wait for keypress

80 NEXT N

The above program should print some random numbers then scroll a few of them in the top left corner of the screen UP. If you then keep pressing a key they will scroll up more and more up to 100 times.

### Юмор из R.O.M.

Просто чтобы доказать, что Dave Corney, автор Opus ROM, обладал чувством юмора: посмотрите на сообщение об ошибке после запуска следующего...

Простой способ — использовать HOLD IT (OUTLET 24). После его загрузки нажмите E, чтобы извлечь две строки, которые затем сохраняются на диск или ленту. Всякий раз, когда вам нужно сохранить экран в памяти программы, вы делаете MERGE этих двух строк и затем используете:

```text
10 LOAD "PICTURE" SCREEN$ : REM сразу после загрузки программы

20 GOSUB 9944 : REM это сохраняет экран в памяти

30 остальная часть программы, которая может очищать экран, печатать на нём что-либо и т.д.....

99 GO SUB 9946: REM это восстановит картинку в любой нужный момент!
```

Что касается WINDOW WINDER (OUTLET 11), вы извлекаете строки кода из основной демонстрационной программы с помощью опции в главном меню и сохраняете этот кусок бейсика. Затем вы при необходимости делаете MERGE в свои программы.

Чтобы использовать подпрограмму для скроллинга части экрана, сначала нужно указать программе, КАКУЮ именно область или «окно» экрана вы хотите скроллить. Это делается с помощью POKE, указанных в инструкции: от 65020 до 65023.

Сделав это, вы вызываете один из RANDOMIZE USR, описанных в руководстве, и область, заданная POKE, сдвинется в одном направлении. Повторяя RANDOMIZE USR, вы скроллите её дальше и дальше. Вот пример...

```text
10 CLEAR (whatever): GO SUB 9930

20 FOR N=1 TO 50: PRINT RND;
   :NEXT N: REM это просто заполняет верхнюю часть экрана числами для теста, вместо этого можно загрузить SCREEN$

30 POKE 65020,0:POKE 65021,0:REM
   верхний левый угол экрана в позиции PRINT 0,0.

40 POKE 65022,10:POKE 65023,10:
   REM задаём размер окна 10 на 10

50 FOR N=1 TO 100

60 RANDOMIZE USR 65000: REM
   скролл ВВЕРХ

70 PAUSE 0:REM ждём нажатия клавиши

80 NEXT N
```

Приведённая выше программа должна напечатать несколько случайных чисел, а затем сдвинуть часть из них в левом верхнем углу экрана ВВЕРХ. Если продолжать нажимать клавишу, они будут сдвигаться вверх всё дальше — до 100 раз.

Стоит отметить, что вместо пометки «by...» («автор...») на клипарте в версии для Spectrum стояло «SENT IN by...» («прислал...»), а в версии для SAM — «FROM...» («от...») (это небольшое расхождение возникло просто потому, что я взял Бейсик от предыдущей программы клипартов для SAM вместо повторной конвертации бейсика со Спектрума). Не было никакого намерения выдать это за собственную работу Криса, и он сам ни разу не утверждал, что это его работа.

Мне жаль, что так вышло, и урок из этого таков: читатели должны быть бдительны и не присылать в OUTLET ничего, если только это не их собственная работа или они точно не уверены, что программа находится в общественном достоянии (FREEWARE). — Brian

### Brian Cavers отвечает D. Graham

Нет, практического способа нет. В теории подключить можно что угодно к чему угодно, но просто чтобы вы понимали... Для +3 потребуется собственный блок питания, так как того, что в Opus, недостаточно, поэтому вам пришлось бы перерезать линию питания на краевом разъеме. После этого их, возможно, удалось бы соединить с помощью аппаратного переходника FIXIT, модифицированного кем-то с глубокими познаниями в электронике и богатым опытом. Но даже тогда всё работало бы только в режиме 48K, и нет никакой гарантии, что оно вообще заработает. Энтузиаст-электронщик мог бы взяться за это ради спортивного интереса, но в противном случае я бы посоветовал оставить эту затею в покое.
